definitionEn: To speak with someone in order to share ideas or information.
example: We talked for hours about our holiday plans over dinner.

definitionEn: To pay attention to a sound or to what someone is saying.
example: Please listen carefully, because the instructions will change soon.

definitionEn: To say or write something as an answer to a question or message.
example: I will reply to your email as soon as I finish this report.

definitionEn: A piece of written or spoken information sent from one person to another.
example: She left a short message on my phone asking me to call back.

definitionEn: A written message sent to someone, usually by post.
example: My grandfather still writes a long letter to me every month.

definitionEn: An act of speaking to someone using a telephone.
example: I received a phone call from my sister during lunch today.

definitionEn: A message sent electronically from one computer or phone to another.
example: Please check your email for the details of the meeting tomorrow.

definitionEn: To talk with someone in a friendly, informal and relaxed way.
example: The two neighbours like to chat over the fence each morning.

definitionEn: To say words aloud in order to communicate with another person.
example: Please speak more slowly so that everyone can follow you.

definitionEn: A system of words and sounds used by a group of people to communicate.
example: Learning a new language takes patience, practice and plenty of courage.

definitionEn: To come together with someone at a particular place and time.
example: Let's meet at the café near the station at seven o'clock.

definitionEn: To say hello to someone when you see or meet them.
example: The receptionist greeted every visitor with a warm smile.

definitionEn: To talk with others about a subject, considering different opinions.
example: We need to discuss the project plan before the meeting on Friday.

definitionEn: To make something clear or easy to understand by giving details.
example: The teacher took time to explain the grammar rule again.

definitionEn: To have the same opinion as someone, or to say yes to a plan.
example: Everyone agreed that the new schedule was fair and easy to follow.

definitionEn: To speak angrily or to give reasons for and against an opinion.
example: The two friends argue about football every time they meet.

definitionEn: To tell others about something or let them use something together.
example: She likes to share her travel photos with friends online.

definitionEn: To know the meaning of what someone has said or written.
example: I did not understand the joke, so I asked her to explain it.

definitionEn: To put a question to someone in order to get information.
example: Do not hesitate to ask me if you have any questions.

definitionEn: To perceive a sound with your ears, or to learn news from someone.
example: We could hear the children laughing from the other room.

definitionEn: A sign, sound or gesture that gives information or a command.
example: The teacher gave a signal, and the whole class stood up quietly.

definitionEn: A movement of the hands, head or body used to express a feeling or idea.
example: He made a friendly gesture by offering me his seat on the train.

definitionEn: A facial expression with upturned lips that shows happiness or friendliness.
example: Her warm smile made every new student feel welcome at once.

definitionEn: The sound produced through the mouth when people speak or sing.
example: I recognised his voice immediately, even over the noisy phone line.

definitionEn: To show or communicate a thought or feeling through words or actions.
example: It is hard to express my gratitude for all your kind help.

definitionEn: To say or do something as a reaction to something that has happened.
example: The company will respond to customer complaints within two working days.

definitionEn: To say that you are sorry for something you did wrong or caused.
example: He apologised for arriving late and missing the start of the talk.

definitionEn: To say that you are unhappy or dissatisfied with something or someone.
example: Several guests complained about the noise from the party upstairs.

definitionEn: To demand something firmly, or to state that something is definitely true.
example: She insisted on paying for lunch, even though we had planned to split it.

definitionEn: To propose an idea or plan for someone to consider.
example: I suggest we meet earlier so that we have more time to talk.

definitionEn: To tell someone a private secret or personal feeling in confidence.
example: She confided in her best friend about her worries for the future.

definitionEn: The quality of a voice or piece of writing that shows the speaker's attitude.
example: I could hear a sharp tone in his voice, so I stayed silent.

definitionEn: The way people pronounce words, which often shows where they come from.
example: Her northern accent made her easy to recognise among the group.

definitionEn: Informal talk about other people's private lives, often without proof.
example: The office was full of gossip about the new manager's plans.

definitionEn: A story passed around among people that may not be true.
example: A rumour spread quickly that the school would close early.

definitionEn: To get in touch with someone by phone, email or letter.
example: Please contact the office if you need further information.

definitionEn: To tell someone about a fact, situation or change in a formal way.
example: We will inform all passengers about the delay as soon as possible.

definitionEn: To say something that removes someone's worry or doubt.
example: The doctor reassured the patient that the test results were normal.

definitionEn: To say what you think is wrong or bad about someone or something.
example: Some critics criticise the film for being too long and slow.

definitionEn: A polite remark that expresses admiration or praise for someone.
example: She gave me a kind compliment on my new haircut.

definitionEn: To make someone agree to do something by giving good reasons.
example: We persuaded our manager to try the new scheduling system.

definitionEn: To stop someone while they are speaking or doing something by speaking.
example: Please do not interrupt me while I am explaining the results.

definitionEn: A formal discussion in which people argue opposing sides of an issue.
example: The debate about the new law lasted for most of the afternoon.

definitionEn: To change words from one language into another while keeping the meaning.
example: She agreed to translate the letter from Vietnamese into English.

definitionEn: Expressing ideas clearly and persuasively, using fluent and forceful language.
example: The eloquent speaker moved the audience with her powerful words.

definitionEn: Honest and open in what you say, even when the truth is unpleasant.
example: She was candid about her mistakes during the team review.

definitionEn: To avoid giving a clear answer, often on purpose and to avoid blame.
example: The manager equivocated when reporters asked about the budget cuts.

definitionEn: Done on purpose and after careful thought, rather than by accident.
example: His pause before answering was deliberate, meant to make them think.

definitionEn: Avoiding a direct answer or clear statement, often to hide the truth.
example: The witness gave evasive replies and would not look at the jury.

definitionEn: The quality of being open, honest and sincere in speech or manner.
example: I appreciated the candour of his feedback on my essay draft.

definitionEn: The art of persuasive speech, or language that sounds impressive but says little.
example: The politician relied on rhetoric rather than facts to win the crowd.

definitionEn: Using more words than are needed, making the message longer and duller.
example: The report was so verbose that nobody finished reading it.

definitionEn: Using very few words, sometimes in a way that seems rude or abrupt.
example: His terse reply made it clear that he was not interested.

meaningVi: nói lộn xộn, làm sai lệch
definitionEn: To confuse or distort a message so that it becomes hard to understand.
example: The poor phone line garbled the directions, so we got completely lost.

definitionEn: To speak with repeated pauses and sounds, often because of nervousness.
example: She began to stammer when the audience asked her a difficult question.

meaningVi: lẩm bẩm, nói nhỏ không rõ
definitionEn: To speak quietly and unclearly, so that others find it hard to hear.
example: He began to mumble his answers, so the teacher asked him to repeat.

definitionEn: To ask for information, especially in a formal or polite way.
example: I would like to enquire about the availability of rooms next week.

definitionEn: To prevent something from happening, or make it impossible in advance.
example: A tight deadline should not preclude a careful and honest review.

meaningVi: ám chỉ, nhắc đến gián tiếp
definitionEn: To mention something indirectly, without stating it clearly.
example: The speaker alluded to the scandal without naming anyone directly.

meaningVi: nói bóng gió, ám chỉ xấu
definitionEn: To suggest something bad indirectly, without saying it openly.
example: The journalist insinuated that the minister had known about the fraud.

definitionEn: To provide evidence or support that confirms what someone has said.
example: Two witnesses corroborate her version of events from that evening.

definitionEn: A quick, sharp reply, often made to answer a criticism or insult.
example: His clever retort made the whole room burst into laughter.

definitionEn: A reply that shows an argument or accusation to be false or wrong.
example: The company issued a rebuttal to the article's claims within an hour.

definitionEn: Intended to make peace or to reduce anger and hostility between people.
example: The director adopted a conciliatory tone to calm the angry staff.

definitionEn: Skilled at handling sensitive matters without causing offence to others.
example: She gave a diplomatic answer that avoided upsetting either side.

definitionEn: Careful not to offend or upset people when speaking about sensitive matters.
example: It was tactful of him to mention the mistake without embarrassing anyone.

definitionEn: Direct and honest in speaking, without hesitation or unnecessary politeness.
example: The forthright manager told us exactly what needed to change.

definitionEn: Suggested or understood without being directly stated or expressed.
example: There was an implicit warning in her calm tone of voice.

definitionEn: Stated clearly and directly, leaving nothing to be guessed.
example: The contract gave explicit instructions about payment and deadlines.

definitionEn: Speaking or writing at excessive length, with too many unnecessary details.
example: The prolix speech tested the patience of everyone in the hall.

definitionEn: A talk, often given in church, that gives moral advice or lessons.
example: The priest's homily focused on kindness and respect for others.

meaningVi: câu châm ngôn, cách nói súc tích
definitionEn: A short, wise saying that expresses a general truth in a memorable way.
example: Her favourite aphorism reminded her to listen before she speaks.

meaningVi: tiếng địa phương, cách nói dân dã
definitionEn: The everyday language or dialect spoken by ordinary people in a region.
example: The novel is written in the vernacular of the working-class city streets.

definitionEn: Specialised words used by a particular group, which are hard for others to follow.
example: The engineers used technical jargon that confused the rest of the team.

definitionEn: A mild or indirect word used in place of one that sounds harsh or unpleasant.
example: Passed away is a common euphemism for died in polite conversation.

definitionEn: A word formed from the first letters of a phrase, such as NATO or UNESCO.
example: Many business emails are full of acronyms that new staff must learn.

definitionEn: Tending to talk a great deal, often at length and with enthusiasm.
example: The loquacious host kept the guests entertained with endless stories.

definitionEn: Reserved and silent, speaking only when necessary.
example: The taciturn farmer answered our questions with only a nod or shrug.

definitionEn: Talking too much, especially about unimportant things in a rambling way.
example: The garrulous taxi driver told us his life story before we arrived.

definitionEn: Using very few words to express meaning, sometimes in a blunt way.
example: His laconic reply, just yes or no, ended the discussion quickly.

definitionEn: The use of many words to say something that could be said more simply.
example: His circumlocution about the budget made the simple fact very hard to find.

definitionEn: Using a roundabout phrase instead of a direct word to express an idea.
example: Using periphrasis, she described the cook as one who feeds the hungry crowd.

definitionEn: Clever but misleading arguments used to deceive people into accepting a false idea.
example: His argument was pure sophistry, designed to hide the obvious mistake.

definitionEn: Subtle reasoning that tries to justify a wrong action by bending moral rules.
example: The lawyer's casuistry made a dishonest deal sound perfectly reasonable.

meaningVi: làm rối rắm, che mờ sự thật
definitionEn: To make something unclear or confusing on purpose, so people cannot understand it.
example: The report seemed to obfuscate the real causes of the losses.

meaningVi: giả vờ, che giấu ý thật
definitionEn: To hide your true thoughts or feelings behind a false appearance.
example: He tried to dissemble his anger with a forced and cheerful smile.

definitionEn: To speak in a way that avoids telling the truth or giving a straight answer.
example: Rather than prevaricate, he should simply admit where the money went.

definitionEn: To persuade someone to do something by gentle flattery or coaxing.
example: The mother tried to cajole the child into eating a few more vegetables.

meaningVi: nịnh nọt để xin, dỗ dành
definitionEn: To gain something from someone through persistent flattery or pleading.
example: The child wheedled a sweet from his aunt by smiling sweetly.

definitionEn: To charm or delight someone, often in a way that makes them lower their guard.
example: The salesman beguiled the customers with stories about his products.

definitionEn: Optimistic and cheerful, especially when facing a difficult situation.
example: Despite the setbacks, she remained sanguine about the project's success.

definitionEn: Sharp and bitter in tone or manner, especially in criticism or wit.
example: The critic's acerbic comments about the play delighted some and angered others.

definitionEn: Bitterly critical or sarcastic in a way intended to hurt someone.
example: Her caustic remark about his haircut silenced the whole table.

definitionEn: Filled with bitter hatred, and expressed in very harsh or cruel language.
example: The vitriolic comments online made the debate painful for everyone.

definitionEn: Harsh, abusive language used to attack or criticise someone angrily.
example: The politician's speech was full of invective aimed at his rivals.

definitionEn: A bitter and forceful verbal attack on a person, idea or institution.
example: The columnist delivered a furious diatribe against the new tax.

definitionEn: A passionate and bitter speech attacking someone, named after ancient Athenian orations.
example: The union leader delivered a long philippic against the company's directors.

definitionEn: Grimly mocking or sneering, showing contempt in an ironic way.
example: With a sardonic smile, he commented that the meeting had been brilliant.

definitionEn: Using humour, irony or exaggeration to criticise people or society.
example: The satirical magazine mocked the government with cartoons each week.

definitionEn: Sweet, soft and pleasant to hear, especially describing a voice or sound.
example: Her dulcet voice soothed the restless children at bedtime.

definitionEn: Deep, full and rich in sound, especially a voice that carries well.
example: The sonorous voice of the speaker filled the entire grand hall.

definitionEn: Sweet and smooth in sound, flowing pleasantly, especially when speaking.
example: The mellifluous narrator read the poem so softly that everyone listened.

definitionEn: Extremely loud and powerful, used to describe a voice that carries a long way.
example: The stentorian shout of the coach could be heard across the whole field.

meaningVi: khàn, phát ra từ cổ họng
definitionEn: Harsh and throaty in sound, produced at the back of the mouth or throat.
example: His guttural growl warned the dogs to stay back from the gate.

meaningVi: du dương, lên xuống nhịp nhàng
definitionEn: Having a light, rising and falling rhythm, typical of a cheerful voice.
example: Her lilting accent made every sentence sound like a happy song.

definitionEn: A speech in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, usually while alone.
example: In the play, the hero delivers a long soliloquy about his fears.

definitionEn: A long speech by one person, which prevents others from taking part in the conversation.
example: He delivered a long monologue, leaving no time for anyone to respond.

definitionEn: A private conversation between two people, away from others.
example: They had a quiet tête-à-tête over coffee after the busy meeting.

definitionEn: A formal conversation or discussion, often between two or more parties.
example: The colloquy between the two governments lasted several days.

definitionEn: Needless repetition of the same idea in different words, such as free gift.
example: Saying the past history is a tautology, since history is already the past.

definitionEn: Pompous language that sounds impressive but has little real meaning.
example: The speech was full of bombast but offered no real plan for reform.

meaningVi: lối nói khoa trương, văn hoa
definitionEn: Lofty, pompous language used to impress the listener rather than inform.
example: The grandiloquence of his toast embarrassed the young couple slightly.

meaningVi: câu nệ tiểu tiết, khoe chữ
definitionEn: Overly concerned with minor rules or details, especially to show off knowledge.
example: The pedantic editor corrected every comma, even in casual messages.

meaningVi: vốn từ, từ điển thuật ngữ
definitionEn: The vocabulary of a language, or the set of terms used within a particular field.
example: The lawyers spoke a dense lexicon that few outsiders could understand.

meaningVi: tiếng lóng, từ ngữ nhóm riêng
definitionEn: Specialised slang used by a particular group or social class, often secretive.
example: The street artists spoke an argot full of playful, coded words.

definitionEn: A particular style or type of language used by a specific group of people.
example: In business parlance, the deal was described as a win-win arrangement.

definitionEn: A particular way of expressing something in words, such as a phrase or idiom.
example: That locution is typical of old-fashioned speech in the countryside.

definitionEn: Lengthy and unnecessary fuss or talk, usually about something simple.
example: Getting the simple form signed involved a long palaver with three offices.

definitionEn: A skilled public speaker who delivers speeches in a powerful and persuasive way.
example: The orator held the crowd spellbound with his passionate words.

definitionEn: To talk at length in a pompous, self-important way that says little.
example: The manager loved to bloviate about his success at every meeting.
